In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution and function of aquaporin isoform in radish tissues.
the tissue- and cell-type specific accumulation of aquaporin isoform and the measurement of the water permeability of protoplasts.
tissue- and cell-type-specific accumulation of aquaporins and their water channel activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aquaporins are not only important for cell-to-cell communication, but are also important for the maintenance of cell homeostasis.
aquaporins are involved in the regulation of water movement in the radish plant.
aquaporins are not only important in the transport of water but also in the regulation of cell growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aquaporin levels are regulated to maintain a constant water flow through the tissues and cells.
the aquaporin isoform distribution is regulated to meet the water requirement of different tissues and cells.
the water channel activities are regulated at the tissue level, and the regulation is controlled at the cell level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water permeability of the plasma membrane of protoplasts is high, regardless of the tissue and cell types.
aquaporins are unevenly distributed in the tissues of the radish, and the water permeability of the individual cells in the root cortex and endodermal layers is high.
the water channel activity is regulated individually in tissues.
